summary:
What happens when an astronaut faces a medical emergency millions of miles from Earth, tangled in wires and separated by a 44-minute Mars communication delay? Developed by Team NOVA GUARDS, Astro-Vitals AI is a contactless AI health monitoring and autonomous 3D medical triage software built for deep-space missions and rural Earth telemedicine.

In space, microgravity fluid shifts, radiation, air fluctuations, and stress cause cardiac strain, bone loss, and ocular SANS. Historically, 1937 wired PPG restricted movement, 1965 NASA wearables caused severe skin irritation over long missions, and 1990s JPL radio sensing struggled with spacecraft vibration noise.

Astro-Vitals AI solves this through a 10-second contactless optical AI (rPPG) camera scan of the face and eyes to extract Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, SpO2, Core Temperature, Sleep, and Mood—while auto-syncing with a wrist blood glucose sensor (mg/dL) and Ultrasound imaging for femur bone density and eye optic nerve monitoring. Calibrated with NASA OSDR and HRP baselines, our interactive 3D Digital Twin isolates organs into Green (nominal), Yellow (autonomous self-care workouts/hydration), and Red (emergency stabilization and Earth alerts), while bringing zero-cost smartphone diagnostics to isolated villages on Earth.
details:
1. What Astro-Vitals AI Does & What Factors Our Team Considered Developed by Team NOVA GUARDS, Astro-Vitals AI is an autonomous, contactless optical health monitoring and 3D medical triage platform built for deep-space missions (Artemis and Mars) and remote Earth telemedicine.

When designing our solution, our team considered two critical operational realities:

  • Spaceflight Physiological Hazards: Microgravity pushes blood toward the upper body (disrupting heart rate and cranial pressure), space radiation stresses blood vessels, cabin air fluctuations trigger sudden oxygen drops, and confinement elevates stress hormones. Furthermore, Mars missions face up to a 44-minute round-trip communication delay, making real-time reliance on Earth flight surgeons impossible during acute medical crises.
    • 1937 (Alrick Hertzman's Traditional PPG): Introduced optical blood volume sensing but required wired sensors that tangle and restrict astronaut mobility in zero gravity.
    • 1965 (Spacelabs & NASA Wireless Telemetry for Edward White): Eliminated long tether cables, yet continuous 24/7 wearable straps and electrodes cause severe skin irritation and disrupt astronaut sleep over multi-month missions.
    • Late 1990s (NASA JPL Radio-Frequency Sensing): Attempted contactless cardiac monitoring via radio waves, but spacecraft mechanical vibrations and crew motion artifacts degraded signal accuracy.

2. How It Works (10-Second Hybrid Clinical Architecture) Astro-Vitals AI overcomes both wearable discomfort and spacecraft vibration noise through a three-layer hybrid workflow:

  • 10-Second Contactless Optical AI (rPPG & Ocular Scan): Using any standard optical camera, our computer vision engine locks onto facial Regions of Interest (forehead and malar skin) and ocular landmarks. By analyzing microscopic green/red light absorption fluctuations in subcutaneous capillary blood flow alongside eye-blink dynamics—and cancelling motion noise via facial landmark tracking—it extracts Heart Rate (BPM), Blood Pressure (mmHg), Blood Oxygen ($SpO_2$), Core Temperature trends, Sleep Score, and Mood/Cognitive Fatigue in just 10 seconds with zero skin contact.
  • Auto-Synced Internal Hardware Link (Wrist Glucose & Ultrasound): Because optical cameras cannot penetrate bone or measure blood chemistry directly, our software automatically links with an onboard Wrist Bio-Sensor for blood glucose monitoring ($\text{mg/dL}$) and a point-of-care Ultrasound (Echography) Probe. Selecting the Eyes or Bones automatically launches full-frame B-mode ultrasound viewports to measure Femur Cortical Bone Mineral Density (BMD T-Score) and Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD in mm) to detect Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).
    • GREEN (Nominal): Vitals are within healthy microgravity baselines.
    • YELLOW (Autonomous Self-Care): Detects early risk (e.g., mild osteopenia, dehydration, hyperglycemia, or stress) and prescribes immediate crew countermeasures—such as exact hydration intake, targeted ARED resistive exercise, or paced breathing.
    • RED (Critical Emergency): Provides immediate onboard stabilization protocols (e.g., oral glucose administration or Lower Body Negative Pressure - LBNP suit activation for severe SANS) while transmitting a high-priority encrypted alert packet to Earth medical control.

3. How Our Project Is Creative

  • Bridging Optical AI with Deep-Tissue Diagnostics: Instead of relying solely on a webcam or solely on bulky wearables, we created a unified hub where contactless rPPG vision works in tandem with auto-synced ultrasound imaging and metabolic glucose tracking.
  • Interactive Single & Multi-Organ Isolation: Our 3D Digital Twin dynamically filters the interface—allowing astronauts under high cognitive load to click and isolate specific systems (such as viewing Ocular SANS and Femur Bone Ultrasound side-by-side in 100% full-frame clarity) without visual clutter.

4. Benefits & Intended Impact (Deep Space & Rural Earth)

  • For Deep Space Exploration: Eliminates skin-irritating wires and wearable straps, enables rapid 10-second daily crew checkups, and empowers astronauts to autonomously diagnose and treat early pathologies during 44-minute Mars communication blackouts.
  • For Earth Telemedicine: Rural villages and isolated mountain communities face the same barrier as deep-space crews: distance from hospitals and lack of expensive diagnostic equipment. Because Astro-Vitals AI's core rPPG engine runs on any standard smartphone or laptop webcam, it delivers zero-cost, 10-second preventive health screening to underserved populations worldwide.

5. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Coding Languages: Python, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Computer Vision & Biometric Signal Processing: OpenCV, Google MediaPipe (Facial Mesh & Ocular Landmark ROI tracking), NumPy, and SciPy (bandpass filtering and Fast Fourier Transform for rPPG waveform extraction).
  • Frontend Interface & 3D Visualization: Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas (real-time B-mode ultrasound simulation and rPPG pulse waveform plotting), Interactive SVG 3D Anatomical Twin, and WebRTC (navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia for live webcam integration).
  • Hardware & Scientific Baselines: Standard Optical Webcam / Smartphone Camera, simulated Point-of-Care Ultrasound (7.5 MHz Linear/Convex Probe) & Wrist CGM telemetry, calibrated using NASA OSDR and NASA HRP datasets.
